### C2. Their Exhibit 6 (the certified deed): the BIR eCARs

Page 2 of their certified copy carries two eCARs for this one sale: one dated **19 June 2020** naming **T-38838** as the title, and one dated **18 November 2021** naming T-52540. Taxes were paid on 15 June 2020. **T-38838 is an earlier title over this same land**: Lot 2-X-6-I, 32,448 sqm, issued 11 April 1996 in Mary Worrick Keesey's name, later subdivided into T-49061 (31,027 sqm) and then T-52540 (around 2000). I hold a certified copy of T-38838. So in 2020 the BIR cleared a 2016 sale under a title superseded some twenty years earlier, and the clearance had to be redone in 2021. **T-38838 is cancelled:** the paper title bears "CANCELLED" stamps referencing T.C.T. No. T-49060 and T.C.T. No. 40713, consistent with the request of 1 March 1999 (PE-226716-25-25) to segregate Lots 2-X-6-I-3 and 2-X-6-I-4 (Psd-05-019929), after the 1996 sales of small portions to Jose Pascual Jr., Roscoe Leaño and Cesar Ramirez. Yet the Registry's computerized record for T-38838 carries the October 2016 Affidavit of Loss, the 1991 SPA, the March 2017 court-ordered duplicate and my mother's 2023 affidavit, under the same entry numbers as on T-52540. So Cesar's 2016–2017 instruments were processed against a title cancelled some seventeen years earlier, and the 2020 eCAR followed suit. Taken together, it suggests the sale was papered without the current title in hand. Questions for their witnesses: why was a 2016 sale first processed in 2020, under a long-cancelled title, and who surrendered Cesar's 2017 replacement duplicate for registration in 2021, four years after his death?

### C5. Building permits for the structures on the lot: the Building Official has refused to produce them

Nothing in our files shows any building or occupancy permit issued to the Balanes for the structures on Lot 2-X-6-I-4-C(-1), Brgy. San Roque (Brgy. 1). **Engr. Erwin H. Balane is the Municipal Engineer and Building Official**, and his office has refused my requests for permit records concerning Barangay 1, including a 2021 subdivision. (Those refusals became the ARTA complaints; I will not mention them on the stand.)

Why it matters: under the National Building Code a permit application must show the applicant's right over the land, a title in his name or the owner's written consent or lease. Whatever the Balanes submitted before 2016, if anything, is evidence of what they then acknowledged about ownership; if nothing was issued, their improvements went up without permits, which bears on any claim to be builders in good faith. And Erwin's own affidavit denies using his office in connection with the sale.

Since a further request from me will be refused and used to paint harassment, I suggest the court's process instead: a **subpoena duces tecum** (Rule 21) to the Office of the Building Official for all building and occupancy permits, applications and supporting documents for structures on the lot, in the names of Efren, Gloria, Erwin or Ferdinand Balane, or a certification of no record. Non-compliance is then a matter for the court, not for ARTA. On his cross, the question "does your office hold permits for your family's structures, and will you produce them?" asked in front of the judge is worth more than any FOI refusal. Sources outside the Balanes' control that show the same facts: the Bureau of Fire Protection (fire safety clearances issued for the structures), CANORECO (the documents on which electric service was connected), and the Barangay 1 clearance records for construction. The Provincial Assessor does not hold copies of the municipal tax declarations, so the declarations on the improvements would also have to come by subpoena to the Municipal Assessor. Your call on timing; it may be better served after my testimony.

_Bautista-Spille v. Nicorp Management_, G.R. No. 214057 (19 Oct 2015): authority to sell land must be express and is strictly construed; _Cosmic Lumber Corp. v. Court of Appeals_, G.R. No. 114311 (1996): an agent's act outside the express grant is void; _Alcantara v. Nido_, G.R. No. 165133 (2010): an unauthorized agent's conveyance of land produces no effect; _Yoshizaki v. The entry is on the page already marked as Exhibit "B" but carries no sub-marking; I would ask that it be marked B-5.

Four facts about that instrument. First, neither SPA gave Cesar any power to partition or subdivide: the 1991 SPA is administration only and the 1992 SPA is a sale to a defined class after consultation; its general clause ("any and every act … requisite, necessary or proper") is the kind of language Art. 1877 confines to administration, and a partition of registered land is an act of strict dominion under Art. 1878. Second, none of the co-owners signed it or knew of it; under Art. 496 partition is "by agreement between the parties," and the parties are the co-owners. Third, its dates do not work: it is dated 15 March 2017, yet the plan it says it follows was surveyed on 8 September 2020 and approved on 6 April 2021 (their own Exhibit 1, page 2, recites both dates), and in Atty. Asis's Book CXXII the Deed of Confirmation dated 28 March 2017 is Doc. No. 115 while this agreement dated 15 March 2017 is Doc. No. 402, so the later act sits 287 entries earlier in the same book. Fourth, Cesar was alive on 15 March 2017 and died on 21 June 2017, so he is the only person who could have purported to sign for the owners; if anyone else signed for them after his death, it is worse than unauthorized.

I have checked every file we hold. The instrument itself is in none of them. The Registry's certified file for Entry No. 2021003236 (Ref. No. 2025001096, which I obtained in February 2025) contains only the LRA plan and the technical descriptions, not the agreement. My records requests to the Registry of 30 September 2020 and 25 February 2025 quoted the entry and asked for the complete transaction records; the agreement was never produced. The subpoena in A6 is the way to get it, together with the notarial registers that will show who appeared before Atty. Asis and when.

**Their best answer on the survey, and ours.** I expect Atty. Ramos to say that the field survey was done in 2006 (Princess's Villafuerte receipt of 29 December 2006 is in their own Exhibit 5, page 1) while Cesar was alive and, in Mrs. Balane's words, "under his management," and that the 2020 plan merely formalized it for LRA approval on the strength of that earlier consent. Four answers, in order of strength. First, consent from Cesar in 2006 was consent from nobody: his authority had been revoked on 15 August 2005, and even the 1992 SPA never contained a power to subdivide or partition. Second, the plan certifies a survey "SURVEYED: September 8, 2020," not 2006; the DENR file (subpoena item c) will show whether it was a re-survey, who requested it, and whether any 2006 plan was ever submitted. Third, the Registry's annotation says the land was subdivided "in accordance with subdivision plan number (LRA) PSD-E2020005406," a number that did not exist until 17 September 2020; if the instrument itself names that plan, it could not have been written on 15 March 2017 whatever happened in the field in 2006, which is why the instrument has to be read and not inferred (subpoena items a and b). Fourth, on 8 September 2020 the registered owners were my mother and her sisters; the engineer certified their "full knowledge and consent" when none of them knew, the only agent was three years dead, and the Balanes were not owners. On the defense's best version the certification is still false as to the owners. I would ask that we present the chronology, the revocation and the absence of any partition power as facts, and the antedating as an inference until the DENR file and the instrument are in hand, so that nothing we say outruns the paper.

Why it matters beyond bad faith: even if the court were to uphold the deed, a buyer of a portion of co-owned registered land holds at most an interest in the co-ownership, and a separate title to a specific, bounded lot can issue only on a partition the co-owners made or the court ordered. None exists. The cancellation of TCT No. 079-2021002126 therefore does not depend on the court first finding the sale void, and I would ask that it be pleaded in the alternative. One limit, which I understand from your earlier advice: this argument is aimed at the 2017 instrument only. We do not question the subdivisions of 1993 to 2000 that produced T-52540, which stands in the co-owners' names and on which the Complaint sues.

### C10. "Builders in good faith": how I understand the defense comes apart

Answer ¶49 invokes Articles 448, 546 and 548 and asks for the price, the real property taxes and arrears, the registration and transfer expenses, the survey expenses and the value of necessary and useful improvements, with retention until paid. Mrs. Balane's excluded affidavit puts the improvements at "at least" ₱100,000. On my reading the defense fails in each of three periods, for different reasons, and I would be grateful for your view.

**Before the deed (1975 to September 2016).** By their own Answer (¶¶40, 43, 44[b]) and all three of their affidavits, the family held the lot as tenants of the owners' administrator. The Supreme Court has held that Article 448, with Article 546, "applies only to a possessor in good faith, i.e., one who builds on land with the belief that he is the owner thereof," and "does not apply where one's only interest is that of a lessee under a rental contract" (_Parilla v. Pilar_, G.R. No. 167680, 30 November 2006). A lessee's improvements fall under Article 1678: at the end of the lease the lessor chooses between paying one-half of their value and letting the lessee remove them, and there is no right of retention. Whatever they built while renting is therefore an Article 1678 matter, at the owners' option, and it is for them to prove which structures date from this period and what they are worth.

**From the deed to registration (September 2016 to November 2021).** They plead ownership by purchase, not tolerance. Judged as buyers, they bought from an agent outside his written authority and never asked the owners (C3, C8); a buyer who fails that inquiry is not in good faith from the day of the deed, and good faith must in any case last until registration (_Duenas v. Metrobank_, G.R. No. 209463, En Banc, 29 November 2022). A builder who is not in good faith "loses what is built ... without right to indemnity" (Article 449); the owner may demand demolition at the builder's expense (Article 450) and damages (Article 451). Only necessary expenses are refundable (Article 546, first paragraph), and only a possessor in good faith may retain the thing until reimbursed. Their 2006 survey receipt, in their own Exhibit 5, says the lot was "owned by the Heirs of Worrick Keesey"; in the year they paid to carve out their lot they wrote down whose land it was.

**After the demand (received 22 August 2025) and the summons.** Good faith, if any, is lost "from the moment facts exist which show that the possessor is not unaware that he possesses the thing improperly" (Article 528). From that date all fruits are owed, including the room rentals their Answer admits (¶27), under Article 549, and anything built or rebuilt is forfeit.

**What they will cite.** _Macasaet v. Macasaet_, G.R. Nos. 154391-92 (30 September 2004) and _Department of Education v. Casibang_, G.R. No. 192268 (27 January 2016), which applied Article 448 to people who built with the landowner's own invitation or permission. No owner here consented to any structure; the only relationship was a lease, which _Parilla_ puts under Article 1678; and ¶49 rests on the deed, not on tolerance.

**The reimbursement list, item by item.** The price: no co-owner received a peso (C6); the claim lies against Cesar's estate, which their own ¶38 calls the party whose "acts, receipts, collections" are "the very foundation" of the case. Capital gains tax, documentary stamp tax, transfer tax with surcharge and interest, and registration fees: expenses of registering a void sale, not expenses necessary to preserve the land. The survey: an expense of the same transaction, incurred to cut the owners' land without their consent. Real property taxes actually paid on the land (¶44[i]): the one necessary expense, refundable on proof by official receipts, without retention. Improvements: Article 1678 before the deed, Article 449 after it. The houses of the other families on the lot are not their improvements at all.

**Evidence I propose we put in.** (1) The building permits, or their absence: the National Building Code (PD 1096, Section 301) requires a permit from the Building Official before any construction, and the application must show the applicant's right over the land. The Building Official is defendant Erwin Balane, and his office refused my request (C5). A subpoena duces tecum to his office for every permit, application, plan and certificate of occupancy for structures on the lot in the names of Efren, Gloria, Erwin, Princess, Jomil or Ferdinand Balane, or a certification of no record, answers the question either way: an application shows what right they claimed and when; no permit means they built outside the law, which no builder in good faith does. (2) The Municipal Assessor's tax declarations on the buildings: owner, date declared, assessed value, against the ₱100,000 they now claim. (3) Dates from sources they do not control: Bureau of Fire Protection clearances, CANORECO connection records, barangay construction clearances, and dated satellite imagery of the lot year by year, which I can print with capture dates. (4) Shirley De Leon (Exh. N): in 2020 Gloria came to her house on the land, said she had bought it, tried to evict her, and the defendants later boarded up her door; other neighbours were treated the same on the claim that Gloria had bought "other portions." (5) Their own Exhibit 5 receipts and ¶27.

**On cross,** if you agree: Erwin, whether his office holds a permit or certificate of occupancy for any structure his family built, who signed as owner, and whether he will produce them; Princess, which structures went up after September 2016, who paid, and under what permit.

**In the judgment,** I would ask that improvements after 29 September 2016 be declared forfeited under Article 449, that necessary expenses be refundable only on proof and without retention, and that the owners' Article 1678 option be reserved for any structure proved to predate the deed. The dossier (Part G) sets this out at section 3.11 with the page references.

### C11. The court: how Judge Cu writes and rules, and where I think this case lands on her method

I have read every signed writing of hers we hold: her four orders in this case (6 February, 11 March, 12 March and 4 September 2026) and her two orders in Criminal Case No. 20-6030 over this same parcel (27 November 2020 and 6 January 2021), plus the pre-trial notice issued in her name. We do not hold the 13 May pre-trial order, any ruling on the motion to admit Mrs. Balane's affidavit or on our summary judgment motion, or the 28 August order (A5). What follows is drawn only from her own words, and I offer it for your correction.

**Her method.** She cites no Supreme Court decision in any of the seven writings. She cites the statute or rule by section and date and works rule, then "considering that," then WHEREFORE, in one-sentence paragraphs, in English. Her dispositive paragraphs carry exact particulars: receipt numbers, amounts in words and figures, bank branch, payee. She announced the governing rules in her first order without being asked (the Amended Rules of Civil Procedure, the Revised Rules on Evidence and the Rules on Electronic Filing) and has never written "Summary Procedure." She gives one indulgence and says so ("Liberally applying the rules of procedure ... No further liberality shall be accorded"), warns of sanctions for incorrect pleadings, makes the calendar "final and intransferable unless the ground for resetting is allowed under the rules," and records whether counsel complied on time. She checks who may act ("has no authority to prosecute this case"). She will undo her own act on a rule: she issued warrants and recalled them forty days later as "prematurely filed," without a word about anyone's motives. She does not characterize parties.

**Where I think she lands.** This is a forecast from seven short writings and nothing more.

1. **The deed.** Put Articles 1874, 1878 and 1898 beside Exhibit "E" paragraph 7 and the 1996 annotation on Exhibit "B," and the question becomes whether Mrs. Balane held a Llamanzares contract to sell and whether the owners were consulted. The record answers no to both. A judge who recalls her own warrants on a rule will declare a deed void on a rule. I expect nullity, with the deed's notarial numbers in the dispositive.

2. **The title.** Article 496 beside Entry No. 2021003236 gives her a second, narrower path (C8): no co-owner made or consented to any partition, so no specific-lot title could issue. I expect cancellation of TCT No. 079-2021002126 and ARP No. GR-2023-II-07-001-00256, each by number, and restoration of the portion to the three owners' names, because that is how she writes orders.

3. **Possession.** Ordered, with a fixed period in words and figures.

4. **Improvements, fruits and damages.** This is where her habits run against us unless we prove dates and amounts. She awards what the record proves and does not characterize parties. I expect forfeiture under Article 449 only for structures we show were built after 29 September 2016; an accounting of fruits ordered in principle but quantified only on evidence; real property taxes refunded only against official receipts; and exemplary damages and attorney's fees only if the exhibits compel a finding of wanton or fraudulent conduct. The permits, the Assessor's declarations and the dated imagery (C10, A7) exist to force that finding.

5. **The counterclaim.** Dismissed, because it rests on the title falling the other way.

6. **Mrs. Balane's affidavit.** The one open coin. She gives one indulgence and ends it. If their motion to admit invoked a rule ground she accepts, she may admit it as that single indulgence; if she treats the late filing as a waiver under the Judicial Affidavit Rule, it stays out. I have prepared to testify either way (A3), and her admissions in it help us more than her denials hurt.

**Where she would rule against us.** On form, before she reaches the merits: the "September 24" and "annotated only in 2021" errors in our own Complaint if we leave them for Atty. Ramos (B1, B2); the incomplete certified copies filed as Exhibits "E" and "H" (C1); any filing that calls this a Summary Procedure case; any appearance that does not show my authority on its face; and any brief that argues both that Article 1922 does not apply and that the 2020 publication was "sufficient warning" under it. I would rather we take each of those off the table ourselves.

**What I will do on the stand to fit her court.** Short answers in English, each tied to an exhibit and page; no characterization of anyone; nothing about her 2020 orders on this parcel. If the defense raises that history against Mrs. King on 11 November, the answer is the acquittal and the Court of Appeals' dismissal, in one sentence.

### C12. The statutes, in plain words: what each side will cite and where I think the court lands

Annex 4 is a full section-by-section map of the provisions each side will put before the court, with the exact words and the exhibit that fits each. Because the judge decides by the text of the section and not by case law (C11), I have tried to set out here, in plain words, the ten collisions and the one word in each that I think decides it.

1. **Can this court cancel the title?** They say attacking a title "collaterally" is forbidden (PD 1529, Section 48). But Section 48 forbids only attacks made in passing in some other case; it allows cancellation "in a direct proceeding." Our Complaint prays for the cancellation of TCT No. 079-2021002126 in its caption, which the judge herself recited in her first order. This is the direct proceeding. The word that decides it: _direct_.

2. **What could Cesar do?** Both sides cite Article 1874: a sale of land through an agent needs written authority, "otherwise, the sale shall be void." They say the 1992 SPA is the writing. It is, and the writing itself limits the sale to people holding Llamanzares contracts to sell or who paid Llamanzares, and only after consulting the owners. The judge will read the writing. The word: _writing_.

3. **Was the Balane sale inside that writing?** They will cite Articles 1900 and 1902: a buyer may rely on the power of attorney "as written" and is not bound by the owners' "private or secret" instructions. Those articles help us: the class and the consultation are not secret instructions, they are the written terms, and they were on the title from 1996. Article 1898 then makes the sale void where the buyer "is aware of the limits," and the registry is what made her aware. They will also cite Article 1911 (the owners "allowed" Cesar to act with full powers). Our answer: from August 2005 the owners' conduct was a written revocation, and Article 1911 creates liability, not a valid transfer of land. The word: _written_.

4. **Void, or merely fixable?** This is their sixth defense: Article 1403 makes an unauthorized contract "unenforceable, unless ratified," and they say the estate ratified by taking the money. Article 1874, the special rule for land sold through an agent, says "void," and Article 1409 says contracts "declared void by law … cannot be ratified." Void beats unenforceable because it is the specific rule, and nothing void can be ratified. The money went to a revoked agent and his son and never reached any owner anyway. The word: _void_.

5. **Does the revocation, or its non-registration, matter?** They cite Article 1921 (revocation does not prejudice the "specified persons" the agent was to deal with unless they were notified) and PD 1529, Section 64 (a revocation "shall be registered"). Article 1921 protects only the specified persons, and the SPA names them; Mrs. Balane was never one, so the revocation is beside the point for her. Section 64 is a direction to register, not a condition of validity, and it only matters for a sale inside the power. And what was registered in 1996 was the SPA itself, limits included (Section 52). The one thing we must not do is argue that the 2020 newspaper notice was Article 1922 "sufficient warning" while also arguing that Article 1922 does not apply; it does not apply, because Cesar's powers were special, not general. The word: _specified_.

6. **Was she a buyer in good faith, and until when did she have to be?** They cite Article 527 (good faith is presumed) and Section 53 (an "innocent holder for value" is protected). Article 526 defines good faith: not "aware" of any flaw in the mode of acquisition. Article 528 says good faith ends "from the moment facts exist" showing awareness. Section 51 makes registration the "operative act," and the Supreme Court reads that to mean good faith must last until registration, which here was 23 November 2021. The facts in that window are dated and on paper: her own 2020 power of attorney to sue over the land, the pleading with the newspaper notice received by her side's lawyer in July 2021, her processor's certified copy of the SPA in August 2021, and her sworn "my property" in September 2021. The judge does not have to call anyone dishonest; she has to find that facts existed. The word: _aware_.

7. **Could a specific lot ever be titled to her?** Article 496: partition is made "by agreement between the parties," and the parties to a partition of co-owned land are the co-owners. No co-owner signed the 2017 partition; no power of attorney ever allowed Cesar to partition; and the partition cites a survey plan that did not exist until 2020. They have no article for this. Even if the court upheld the deed, the title falls here. The word: _parties_.

8. **What about the houses?** They cite Articles 448 and 546: a builder "in good faith" is paid for improvements and may stay until paid. Both articles turn on the words "in good faith," which Article 526 defines. Before the deed they were renters by their own Answer, and a renter's improvements fall under Article 1678 (the owner pays half their value or lets the renter remove them; no right to stay). After the deed they were buyers who never asked the owners, and a builder not in good faith "loses what is built … without right to indemnity" (Article 449) and may be made to demolish at his expense (Article 450); only expenses of preservation are refunded (Article 452). The word: _renting_, in their own Answer.

9. **Rents and damages.** They cite Article 544 (a good-faith possessor keeps the fruits). Article 549 makes a bad-faith possessor return them, and their Answer admits rooms were rented. Exemplary damages need a finding that they acted in a "fraudulent" or "oppressive" manner (Article 2232); this judge will not make it on an impression, so we prove it by five dated documents: the deed's "in hand paid" against receipts to February 2017; the 2016 petition that hid the sale and listed a title cancelled in 1999; the 2017 partition under a 2020 plan; the 2020 survey certified with the "consent of the owners" when the only agent was dead; the 2021 "my property" over land titled to three other people. Attorney's fees follow (Article 2208). The word: _fraudulent_, proved by dates.

10. **Their counterclaim.** It rests on the suit being malicious. A suit that succeeds on title cannot have been malicious, and the agency referrals they call harassment are the agencies' own acts. The counterclaim stands or falls with the title (Rule 6, Section 7).

Three words carry the case on her method: **void** (Article 1874), **aware** (Article 526) and **parties** (Article 496). A fourth sits inside the class clause itself: **therefor** (a down payment is paid _for a sale_, and a sale needs an object and a price; C13). Each is on the page of an exhibit already in the record. Annex 4 sets out the full text of every provision above and the procedural rules she enforces, with her own words beside each.

### C13. The class clause, word by word, and what a "downpayment" requires

Paragraph 7 of the SPA reads: "in favor of third persons in possession of CONTRACTS TO SELL executed by the previous administrator, MR. BEN LLAMANZARES and/or to those who have paid their downpayments or have made partial payments therefor to the latter." As I read it, and as I will answer if asked:

1. **Two sub-classes, both tied to one named man.** Holders of a written contract to sell from Llamanzares; and persons who had paid Llamanzares a down payment or partial payment. "In possession of" takes "CONTRACTS TO SELL" as its object, which is what the next words say Llamanzares "executed"; reading it as possession of the land requires deleting the words that follow. "Therefor" means for the sale, so rent is not a payment under the clause; their own receipts say "Payment for the month of." "The latter" can only be Llamanzares, so every receipt signed by Cesar's son, the earliest in October 2003, is outside it. "Have paid … have made" closes the class on 16 March 1992. Paragraph 6's "interested third parties" is the purpose; paragraph 7 begins "Accordingly" and is the operative grant.

2. **A "downpayment" presupposes a sale with an object and a price.** "There is no contract unless … consent … object certain … [and] cause" concur (Art. 1318). A sale requires "a determinate thing" and "a price certain" (Art. 1458); the thing must be "particularly designated or physically segregated from all others of the same class" (Art. 1460); the sale exists only on "a meeting of minds upon the thing … and upon the price" (Art. 1475); earnest money is "part of the price and … proof of the perfection of the contract" (Art. 1482). So the second sub-class is the same people as the first at an earlier documentary stage: persons who had agreed with Llamanzares on an identified portion and a price and had begun paying. On the defendants' own evidence no object or price existed in Llamanzares's time: the portion was first segregated by the survey they paid for in December 2006 (their Exhibit 5, page 1, "lot owned by the Heirs of Worrick Keesey"); "Lot Area: 2,587" first appears on a receipt of 7 August 2016; and the price of ₱250,000 was fixed by Cesar (Mrs. Balane's excluded affidavit, S33). A ₱3,000 payment in the 1980s with no lot, no price and no receipt is money handed to the administrator, which on their own Answer is what rent was.

3. **Whose burden.** Membership is their fourth affirmative defense (¶40) and their first three good-faith circumstances (¶44[a] to [c]); an affirmative allegation is proved by the party making it (Rule 131, Sec. 1), and the buyer claiming good faith carries the burden anyway. They must produce a Llamanzares contract or an agreed portion and price with Llamanzares before 16 March 1992. They have produced neither.

4. **What they have instead.** Three accounts that do not match: ₱3,000 in the 1980s, no receipt, recorded in Manuel Violeta's "brown columnar book" said to have gone "to Cesar and then the Agcaoili Law Office" (Mrs. Balane, S20 to S24, excluded); "already paid" by about 1992 (Salvador, S14 to S15); and the only receipt marked "Down payment," ₱20,000 on 6 January 2005 to Salvador. Nothing shows the pleaded ₱3,000 "credited" in the 2016 price. Two things I will run down: whether the Agcaoili office ever received any Violeta ledger (if it did and it names a Balane, they gain a document; if it did not, her sworn account of where it went is wrong), and the Llamanzares-era sales recorded on the T-4497 title itself (the 1977 "Deeds of Final Sale" by "Mary Worrick-Keesey, thru her Atty.-in-fact Benjamin Llamanzares"), which show what a member of the class looked like: a registered instalment buyer with a registered deed.

5. **My mother's own sworn reading.** Her affidavit of 22 February 2023 (¶4) describes the 1992 authority as "limited authority to perfect the sale of portions of said property in favor of those who already possessed Contract to Sell, or have had made down/partial payment to Benjamin Llamanzares." Salvador's 25 November 2025 letter says the same from the other side (C9).

6. **Cross questions this supports** (for Salvador and Princess): which lot, at what price, agreed with whom, and when; where is the ₱3,000 credited; produce the Violeta book or say where it is.

**A10. My mother's testimony, and three fixes to the proposed judgment.** The second-chair review of our papers makes four points I agree with. (a) Only my mother can give first-hand evidence that no one ever consulted the owners, that no owner received any payment, and what her affidavit of loss of 22 February 2023 meant; on cross I can only say what I know. The Complaint (¶63) reserved her as Exhibit "O". If the pre-trial order kept that reservation, may we file her judicial affidavit five days before 4 November or 2 December and ask the court to take her testimony from California by videoconference under the Supreme Court's videoconferencing guidelines (A.M. No. 20-12-01-SC), or by deposition under Rule 23 before a consular officer? (b) Now that I have testified, a supplemental affidavit from me means recalling me, which needs leave under Rule 132, Section 9; I would rather the same facts came in through her. (c) The proposed judgment (dossier Part 6; playbook 5.4) now (i) directs the Registry to issue a new title over Lot 2-X-6-I-4-C-1 in the three owners' names in lieu of the cancelled one, so the lot is not left untitled; (ii) awards temperate or compensatory damages for the use of the lot from 22 August 2025 before any exemplary damages, because Article 2234 requires that predicate; and (iii) rests the bad-faith finding only on the defendants' own pleading and instruments (their tenancy admissions, the 28 May 2020 SPA, their Exhibit 7's August 2021 Registry copy of the SPA, and the 15 September 2021 "my property" SPA), not on the neighbour's July 2021 pleading, so it stands even if that notice is never imputed to Mrs. Balane. (d) Jurisdiction: Exhibit "D" states the current assessed value as ₱257,670 (tax effectivity 2024), within the ₱400,000 limit; the ₱200,750 figure is the previous value. Your view on each?

**A9. Our Reply ¶14 needs to be restated before the defense reads it.** Our Reply of April 2026, ¶14, answered their Article 1921 defense by saying the 1992 agency "was not created for the purpose of dealing with the defendants specifically or with any other specified persons." The second clause contradicts the class theory, which depends on the SPA naming specified persons: the Llamanzares class. Could the memorandum (or the next filing that touches Article 1921) restate it as: Article 1921 protects only the persons the agency was entrusted to deal with; the SPA names that class; the defendants are outside it; on either reading Article 1921 gives them nothing? I would rather we say it first.

Latagan_ is dated 22 June 2015; _Central Surety_ and _Ciruelas_ are flagged as double-edged; _Alcantara_ is used only for Article 1874's "void." Items for you:
